extraction.name: LUMA
extraction.description: A benchmark multimodal dataset for learning from uncertain data, featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes. It extends CIFAR-10/100 with audio samples extracted from three audio corpora and text data generated using the Gemma-7B Large Language Model. The dataset enables controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty and is accompanied by a Python package for generating multiple dataset variants.
extraction.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier
extraction.citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR ’25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled from multiple sources across three modalities. Images were taken from CIFAR-10/100, with 42 classes selected to ensure at least 600 samples per class after alignment and 8 classes kept as OOD samples; EDM diffusion-generated images were additionally included to alleviate limited image counts for diversity control. Audio samples were collected by extracting pronunciations of CIFAR class labels from The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice using alignments or forced alignments, plus 73 additional voluntary recordings from colleagues. Text samples were generated with Gemma-7B Instruct using 13 prompts per class, then validated by masking label occurrences and asking the same model to classify the text into one of the labels. The modalities were aligned so each text passage relates to the object in the corresponding image and each audio recording is the pronunciation of the object label.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Image data came from CIFAR-10/100 and additional EDM diffusion-generated images. Audio data came from The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, Mozilla Common Voice, and 73 voluntarily contributed recordings from colleagues. Text data was generated using Google's Gemma-7B Instruct model based on class labels.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset package supports controlled manipulation of uncertainty through adjustable parameters including data diversity, sample-level noise, label corruption, and injection of out-of-distribution samples. Data diversity is controlled by extracting deep features from each modality and sampling points based on inverse distance to class centers raised to a parameter k. Label noise is injected by randomly selecting samples and reassigning labels to the class with the lowest mean distance among nearest samples in deep feature space. OOD samples are drawn from held-out classes from the same dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio samples were extracted from aligned or force-aligned transcripts after extending class labels with plural forms where pronunciation changes were minimal. Audio was automatically validated using Whisper Large V3 transcription; samples whose transcription matched the class label or plural form were accepted, while negative predictions were manually validated. Voluntary recordings were anonymized and trimmed. Text samples were generated with Gemma-7B Instruct and validated by masking label occurrences and reclassifying the masked text with the same model; only matching predictions were accepted. For bias reduction in the labels man, woman, boy, and girl, prompts were reconstructed with explicit topics and occupation-related keywords, followed by another round of bias detection. Images were aligned with other modalities and supplemented with EDM-generated images for diversity control.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual annotation was used for audio validation on samples flagged after automatic validation. Annotators were shown an audio sample with the prompt: "Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra 's' or 'es' in the pronunciation is okay.)" and answered Yes or No. Two annotations were collected per sample from 17 annotators. Samples where both annotators confirmed validity were accepted, and samples with conflicting annotations were rejected. Text validation and bias detection were performed automatically using Gemma-7B Instruct, and audio automatic validation used Whisper Large V3 transcription.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For audio manual validation, 2 annotations per sample were collected from 17 annotators, yielding 71.61% annotation agreement. Samples with both annotators confirming validity were accepted, while samples with conflicting annotations were rejected. For automatic audio validation, the authors assumed false positives from Whisper Large V3 were quite low and therefore did not manually validate positive predictions. For text, generated samples were validated by masked-label classification with Gemma-7B Instruct. Bias analysis of generated text was also performed with Gemma-7B Instruct, but the authors state they are unable to assess how accurate or consistent these detections truly are.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 17 annotators; colleagues including M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors, with advanced to fluent English knowledge
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI Whisper Large V3, Gemma-7B Instruct
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available as a Hugging Face dataset and as a Python package with code and instructions on GitHub. The paper states that the dataset can be easily extended with additional modalities and augmented with more data samples, and that the open-source data compilation pipeline and code facilitate community contributions. The authors also plan to include dependent modalities in the future.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender-related terms and attributes are present in generated text data for classes such as man, woman, boy, and girl. Audio data includes diversity of accent in pronunciation. The paper also mentions that 73 voluntary recordings from colleagues were anonymized.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote and support the development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches, especially for safety-critical applications. The authors anticipate that LUMA will help the research community design more trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors performed additional bias analysis and found offensive biases and stereotypes in generated text samples, particularly substantial gender bias for the classes man, woman, boy, and girl. They used Gemma-7B Instruct to detect gender, racial, religious, or cultural biases and found high levels of gender bias in those four classes. They attempted to reduce bias by reconstructing prompts with explicit topics and occupation-related keywords, but report that a significant amount of bias still exists. They also note that LLM-based bias detections could not be assessed for accuracy or consistency.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset modalities are independently sourced, which reflects real-world conditions but may introduce modality-specific uncertainties. Audio extracted from forced alignments may contain misaligned segments, and voluntary audio contributions may include noisy or strongly accented samples that are hard to interpret. Textual data generated using an LLM may contain factual inaccuracies or biases. The authors explicitly state that LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information. They also note limitations of some baseline uncertainty methods for OOD detection on this dataset.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data, uncertainty quantification, robustness analysis, and out-of-distribution detection. Each generated version consists of 500 samples per class for training and 100 for testing across 42 in-distribution classes, plus 3,859 OOD data points from 8 remaining classes. It is intended to support development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches.
